query: Why am I so tired in a way sleep doesn't fix?

per_question.q: Why am I exhausted even though I sleep eight hours?
per_question.why: A's quantity-vs-quality distinction and apnea micro-arousals directly answer the literal question; B presumes an emotional cause.

per_question.q: What blood tests should I ask my doctor for if I'm always tired?
per_question.why: A gives a named panel (ferritin with CRP, TSH + free T4, B12, HbA1c) and the follow-up question to ask when labs come back 'normal'; B has nothing like it.

per_question.q: Is adrenal fatigue a real condition?
per_question.why: A cites the 2016 Cadegiani & Kater systematic review and the Endocrine Society position, then salvages the reader's real symptoms; B never addresses it.

per_question.q: Why do I feel drained for hours after seeing my family even when nothing bad happened?
per_question.why: B's account of the childhood role reactivating at adult prices is the exact mechanism; A has no relational-cost treatment.

per_question.q: Why do I feel guilty whenever I try to rest?
per_question.why: B explains rest-guilt as worth attached to output or caregiving, and stillness as where feeling arrives; A does not cover it.

per_question.q: Could it be sleep apnea if I'm slim, female, and don't snore?
per_question.why: A details the atypical female presentation and the cheap home sleep test; B mentions apnea only in a rule-out paragraph.

per_question.q: Is my exhaustion burnout or depression?
per_question.why: A's burnout/depression/PEM table with WHO ICD-11 status and the exercise-response discriminator is the authoritative version; B's own table is good but adds no evidence base.

per_question.q: Why do I cry at films but feel nothing about my own life?
per_question.why: B's safe-container explanation (a story needs nothing from you afterward) is unique and directly answers the question.

per_question.q: How long after starting iron or thyroid treatment should I expect to feel better?
per_question.why: A gives concrete lag times (8-12 weeks for iron, 6-8 weeks per thyroid dose) and the stop-at-the-reference-floor failure mode; B has no treatment-recovery content.

per_question.q: Why does a five-minute phone call with my mother wipe me out for the day?
per_question.why: B's FAQ answers this verbatim with the activation-cost mechanism; A's frame cannot touch it.

intent_match: A. The query is an open why-question from someone whose sleep has stopped working; the true intent space spans medical, psychiatric, and emotional causes. A answers with the actual differential (sleep quality, oxygen/metabolic limits, load-and-recovery mismatch), the tests that separate it, and red flags — honest coverage of why. B commits to one hypothesis (emotional depletion from vigilance, suppression, caregiving) and serves that subset deeply, but presumes the answer the query is asking for.

A: No treatment of hypervigilance, suppression, or compulsive caregiving as fatigue generators
No explanation of why rest produces guilt rather than relief
No account of why closeness and family contact are the most expensive contexts
No self-observation exercise aimed at the emotional column (B's drain ledger has no counterpart)
Emotional/relational exhaustion covered only as one row in a differential table
B: No actual differential: apnea, iron, thyroid, blood sugar, medication effects reduced to one rule-out paragraph
No tests to request and no guidance for when 'normal labs' is an incomplete answer
No red-flag list for fatigue that needs urgent attention
No post-exertional malaise, perimenopause, ADHD burnout, or long COVID coverage
No verdicts on popular remedies and supplements readers will ask about
Zero external research citations; provenance rests on one unverifiable personal anecdote

first_screen: B. The waking-up-still-working scene plus the verbatim inner sentences is the stronger mirror for this searcher and earns the scroll; A's first screen is a competent but clinical three-bucket summary.
provenance: A. Named systematic review with screened-study counts, institutional positions (Endocrine Society, IOM, CDC, WHO), named cohort studies, and a medical disclaimer. B offers no sources at all and leans on an unverifiable personal narrative (five years, 5,000 hours, seminars abroad).
